findings.defect: The second sufficient condition "or if one of Vmax, Vmin is empty, then M(p,0) decides every such vertex" is FALSE for Vmin = empty, and with it the contrapositive clause "every instance on which M(p,k) stalls has both players present".
findings.evidence: Counterexample, exact arithmetic (/tmp/.../paper-audit-hybrid/a5_dicho.py, a28.py): G = WD(4,2,6) of def:wedge (N=21, stopping, Vmin=empty, w*(v_i)=w*(a_{i,1})=1/2, w*(b_i)=31/64), sigma_0 : v_i -> b_i, p=0. Then val_{sigma_0}(v_i)=7/16, val_{sigma_0}(a_{1,1})=113/256, tau is vacuous so U=val^tau=w* and L=val_{sigma_0}. Every entry rem:own-successor reads at v_1 is strictly positive: Delta_0(v_1,a_{1,1})=15/256, Delta_0(a_{1,1},v_1)=1/16, Delta_0(v_1,b_1)=1/16, Delta_0(b_1,v_1)=3/64; the pair entries are Delta_0(b_1,a_{1,1})=11/256 and Delta_0(a_{1,1},b_1)=1/16. Same at v_2 by the index automorphism, and on WD(6,3,7) (Delta_0(b_1,v_1)=..., all positive). So M(0,0) decides NEITHER value-distinguishing Max vertex. Cause: with Vmin=empty the proof identifies U=w* by the O(N) test TU=U, but L=val_{sigma_p} is still not exact, so Delta_0 = U-L is not D. The Vmax=empty half is correct (sigma vacuous gives val_sigma=w*, then val^tau=w* by the theorem's own first part). Downstream: rem:wedge (line 10620) draws exactly this broken inference ("WD is one-player, so by thm:seed-dichotomy the seeded calculus decides both Max vertices at slack round zero"); its conclusion is nevertheless true for p>=1, since from each of the four profiles of WD(4,2,6) and WD(6,3,7) one all-switches round reaches Opt and M(1,0) then fires at both vertices in both directions (a26.py). The residue in rem:frontier-moved (a stalling instance is one on which switch-all has not converged after p rounds) follows from the FIRST sufficient condition alone and is untouched.

findings.defect: The table of "guaranteed-undecided round counts" is wrong in 6 of its 10 entries: it reports max{k : M_k > 0} (the last round at which P_k is nonempty) instead of max{k : Lambda(P_k)(B_i,A_i) >= 0}, which is what thm:hybrid-lower actually guarantees.
findings.evidence: thm:hybrid-lower gives Delta_k(B_i,A_i) >= Lambda(P_k)(B_i,A_i) = -gamma + 2u(1-u)M_k, nonnegative exactly while M_k >= gamma/(2u(1-u)) = 2^{-L-m-1}/lambda. Exact computation (a17.py, a18_ccert.py) of M_k = lambda^k(1/2+2^{-m}) - 2^{-m}: correct counts are m=2: 1,3,7,16,34 and m=4: 2,7,15,33,68; printed are m=2: 1,3,8,17,34 and m=4: 3,7,16,34,69, which coincide exactly with max{k : M_k > 0}. Directly: last k with Lambda(P_k)(B_1,A_1) >= 0 is 1,3,7 for CC(1,2),CC(2,2),CC(3,2) and 2,7 for CC(1,4),CC(2,4). The certificate ITSELF is confirmed (a18_ccert.py): for those five (L,m) every vertex of every P_k lies in Q(CC(L,m)), every clause of def:slack at Lambda(P_k) dominates Lambda(P_{k+1}) at all N^2 pairs (0 failures), and Delta_k >= Lambda(P_k) against a real hybrid run. The doubling in L and the 2^{Omega(N)} conclusion are unaffected.

findings.defect: "under the operative own-successor test of rem:own-successor every one of these instances is decided at round 2 exactly" is wrong: G_8, H_m, S and S_r are all decided at round 1.
findings.evidence: My engine (a13.py) and the project's own ownhyb.py (a14.py) agree: first own-successor firing round is 1 on G_8, S, S_2, S_5, H_3, H_5 (and 1 on H_4, H_6, S_3..S_10). E.g. on S_r, Delta_1(b_0,v) = -2^{-r-2} < 0 (clause (ii)) -- printed values -1/16 at r=2, -1/128 at r=5; on G_8, Delta_1(4,5) = -1/10; on H_3, Delta_1(h,v) = -1/16. Only R needs round 2, and only at vertices 1 and 4 (vertex 6 fires at round 1), exactly as item (d) says. The pair-test counts in (a),(b),(c) are all correct: G_8 hybrid 1 vs slack 7 vs trans 6; H_m hybrid 1 vs slack 14,38,100,249 vs trans 9,13,17,21; S and S_r hybrid 2 vs slack 12,25,52,104,210 vs trans 8,11,15,18,22.

findings.defect: "whose maximum of x_1 is 1, attained only at u" (both games) and the statement's "THE maximiser of x(v_1)" are false: the optimal face is two-dimensional in both.
findings.evidence: Exact LP over Q(W_10) and Q(W_14) (a6_lasserre.py): on W_10 the face x_1 = 1 is {1} x [7/8,1] x [0,1/4]; on W_14 it is {1} x [7/8,1] x [7/8,1]. So u=(1,7/8,1/4) and u=(1,7/8,7/8) are maximisers, not the unique ones. Everything else in the theorem recomputes exactly (a6, a7): both games stopping, w*(v_1,v_2,v_3) = (1/2,1/2,1/4) and (1/2,1/2,15/32), the stated harmonic normal forms, S positive definite with leading minors 525/64, 35775/4096, 42525/16384 and 175/128, 3975/16384, 1575/131072, the moment matrix PSD, and L(q_v) = 0 at all three controlled vertices in both games (v_1: 3/32 - 3/32 = 0 and 1/64 - 1/64 = 0; v_2, v_3: 0 + 0). The conclusion "the lift improves the bound by nothing" survives, since it needs only u_1 = 1.

findings.defect: The step "the atoms of Pi interpret at (m,k) as (m,h),(g,h),(k,k),(k,h), each in the base or on the diagonal" needs the diagonal to be IN the base, which def:lmc only permits ("at most the diagonal in addition"), not requires.
findings.evidence: If the base is exactly (Z_0 x V) u (V x Z_1) then (k,k) is not a base pair (w*(k)=1/2, so k is in neither Z_0 nor Z_1 of K_#: Z_0 = {t_0}, Z_1 = {g,h,m,t_1}, verified in a1_matching.py). Repair, which I verified: if the clause A contained in Pi that derives (5,1) omits the atom (x^(1),y) then its three atoms at (m,k) are (m,h),(g,h),(k,h), all in V x Z_1, and (m,k) is derived; if A contains (x^(1),y) then (1,1) is derived in G_8 by some clause B assigned to frame(1,1), and frame(k,k) = frame(1,1) (both of types (avg,avg,t_0,avg,avg,t_0) with equality pattern {x=y, x^(0)=y^(0), x^(1)=y^(1)}, computed in a1_matching.py), where B's admissible atoms interpret as (k,h),(h,h),(t_0,k),(t_0,h),(t_0,t_0), all in the base since h is in Z_1 and t_0 in Z_0; so (k,k) is derived either way. One sentence closes the gap. Separately, the chain argument is written only for a chain of length two; a general chain 4 = v_0 <= ... <= v_n = 1 reduces to it by taking the first i with v_i = 1, whence v_{i-1} is in {4,5}.

findings.defect: The statement derives "every sound local matching calculus stalls on G_8" from the pair test alone -- underivability of (4,1) plus unsoundness of (1,4) -- which by rem:own-successor is the wrong test; the own-successor route through (5,1) is closed only inside the transitive-closure paragraph (and by the step flagged above).
findings.evidence: w*(5) = w*(1) = 1/2 in G_8 (a1_matching.py), so (5,1) is value-true and, by rem:own-successor clause (i) at a Max vertex, deriving it would prove successor 1 optimal and decide vertex 5. The theorem's stated chain does not mention (5,1). rem:own-successor's own re-examination list (lines 9421-9433) covers prop:simorder-stalls but not thm:matching-barrier, so the reader is not told where the own-successor case is handled.

findings.defect: Off-by-one: with Q^H_k := K(Delta'_k) one has Delta_{k+1} = Lambda(Q^H_k), not Delta_k = Lambda(Q^H_k).
findings.evidence: def:hybrid sets Delta'_k := C(min(Delta_k, L Delta_k)) and Delta_{k+1} := C(min(Delta'_k, P(Delta'_k))); the lemma's own two redundancy arguments then give Delta_{k+1} = P(Delta'_k) = Lambda(K(Delta'_k)) = Lambda(Q^H_k). lem:wedge-face (line 10349) silently uses the corrected indexing ("let R_k := K(Delta'_{k-1}) be the polytope round k optimises over ... Delta_k = Lambda(R_k) by lem:hybrid-cutting"), so no downstream result is wrong.

findings.defect: The formula w*(b_i) = 1/2 - 2^{-(r-i)-2} is stated with no range for i and is false at i = r+1, a vertex the family has.
findings.evidence: b_{r+1} -> (t_1,t_0) so w*(b_{r+1}) = 1/2, while the formula gives 1/2 - 2^{-1} = 0. Verified for r = 2..7 (a8_transport.py): the formula is correct for 0 <= i <= r (w*(b_0) = 7/16, 15/32, 31/64, 63/128, 127/256, 255/512). All the other numbers of the theorem recompute exactly: Sep(a,b_0) = 5/16, 13/32, 29/64, 61/128; Sep(b_0,a) = 1/16, 1/32, 1/64, 1/128; Sep(v,b_0) = -2^{-r-2}; t_rev = 7/12, 15/28, 31/60, 63/124; and u_k(v) stays above t_rev far beyond 2^{r-2} (first drop at k = 24 for r = 3, beyond 39 for r = 4,5).

findings.defect: Its L(1) = 5/16 is not the L of prop:pdc-separation, which is 11/32, so "no sound upper bound decides that vertex from the SAME lower bound L" cites prop:bracket(a) for a different L.
findings.evidence: Exact computation on the 31-vertex game (a3_pdc.py): with sigma = (0 -> 2, 4 -> 16), val_sigma(1) = 5/16 while prop:pdc-separation's L := max{val_sigma, val_rho} has L(1) = 11/32. Both propositions are internally right; the cross-reference is not literal. The conclusion survives a fortiori since 5/16 < 11/32 < 23/64 = w*(2). Everything else in the item is exact: U(2) = 3/8, Delta_3(2,1) = -1/8 (sequence 1/16, 3/64, 3/64, -1/8), and the own-successor test at vertex 0 fires at k = 3.

findings.defect: The stated reason -- "at M(0,0), since |Vmax| = 1 makes the evaluated bracket exact" -- is false; the bracket is not exact from the wrong sigma, though the vertex is still decided.
findings.evidence: On H_3 with sigma(v) = h (a2_seeded.py): L = val_sigma has L(v) = 1/2 while w*(v) = 9/16, so (L,U) is not exact; the vertex is decided at k = 0 nonetheless, by clause (i) (Delta_0(v,c_1) = U(v) - L(c_1) = 9/16 - 9/16 = 0) and by the pair entry Delta_0(h,c_1) = 1/2 - 9/16 = -1/16. Same at m = 4. |Vmax| = 1 does not make val_sigma exact; what makes U exact is Vmin = empty.

findings.defect: "every controlled vertex of the game G* of prop:simorder-stalls" is unquantified: no (p,k) is given, and the last vertex needs many rounds.
findings.evidence: Exact runs (a4_gstar.py, a4b.py) over all 8 Max profiles: from the all-first-successor sigma, M(0,k) fires at vertices 2,4 at k=5, at 0,1,3 at k=6, at 6 at k=7, and at the Min vertex 5 only at k=17; from sigma = (1,0,0) the last is k=12; from sigma = (1,0,1) and (1,1,1) all seven fire at k=0. So the claim is true only for k >= 17 with the natural starting profile.

findings.defect: The second, larger witness is asserted without being exhibited, against the manuscript's own standard that every negative claim carry an explicit instance; and the hill-climb claim does not say what the generator varied.
findings.evidence: "one of them, on thirteen non-sink vertices, has values 5/12, 11/12, 23/24 and leaves all four of its controlled vertices undecided" -- no edge list, no vertex types, no seed, no generator. Likewise "hill climbing on the fraction of value-distinguishing controlled vertices left undecided reaches 1 within a few hundred stopping games from several independent starts". The explicit 10-vertex witness R of prop:own-stall itself is fully reproducible and I confirmed every number in it (a9_ownstall.py): stopping; w* = (1/2,1/2,1/2,3/4,1/2,1/2,0,1/2); Z_0 = {6,t_0}, Z_1 = {t_1}; value-distinguishing controlled vertices exactly {1,4,6}; and all six own-successor separators equal 0, both with and without the free Z seed.

findings.defect: "thm:hybrid-complete uses the linear programme only through the 4N values ..." is not literally true of Step 5, which invokes Delta <= P(Delta) at a general pair.
findings.evidence: Steps 1-4 use only the four sink families. Step 5 as written concludes Delta(x,y) <= val(x) - val(y) from closedness under P at (x,y). The sink-only variant still gets there through the min-plus closure that def:hybrid already applies: Delta(x,y) <= Delta(x,t_0) + Delta(t_0,y) <= U(x) - L(y) = val(x) - val(y). That sentence is missing. (The corollary's conclusion is correct; the sink-only variant does decide, verified at a25.py.)

findings.defect: "the optimal value of a feasible bounded linear programme is continuous in the right-hand side" is false in general; the correct argument in this situation is monotone.
findings.evidence: An LP optimal value is concave and nondecreasing in the RHS, hence continuous only on the relative interior of its feasibility domain; it can jump at the boundary. Here Delta_k decreases to Delta_infinity, so K(Delta_k) is a decreasing sequence of nonempty compacta (nonempty by soundness) with intersection K(Delta_infinity), and the max of a continuous function over them converges. That is what should be said.

findings.defect: Stated for an infinite chain P_0 ⊇ P_1 ⊇ ... of NONEMPTY compact convex sets, but both applications (thm:hybrid-lower, thm:wedge-proved) use a chain that is nonempty only while M_k >= 0.
findings.evidence: In thm:hybrid-lower, Xi_k is empty as soon as M_k < 0 (e.g. M_2 = -1/16 on CC(1,2)); in def:wedge-chain, P_k is empty once M_k < 0. The induction in the proof is finite, so the applications are legitimate, but the theorem should be stated for a finite chain P_0 ⊇ ... ⊇ P_K with the clause condition at k = 0..K-1.

findings.defect: One case of the clause condition is asserted, not proved: "The Vmax x Vmax composites reduce to the same estimate through max_i min_j <= min_j max_i and the branch a_{1,1}, and need only e >= 2j-2."
findings.evidence: I verified it numerically instead (a21c.py, wcert3.out): over exactly the 60 triples the paper names (j in 2..6, e in {2j-1,2j,2j+1,3j}, m in {j+2,j+4,j+6}), with P_k computed as the true polygon of def:wedge-chain and capped at k <= 15, every clause of def:slack at Lambda(P_k) dominates Lambda(P_{k+1}) at all N^2 pairs, every vertex of every P_k lies in Q(WD), 0 failures in all 60. Also confirmed for all 60: lem:wedge-verts's six-vertex form set(P_k) = {(0,0),(mu,0),(M_k,M_{k+1}),(M_k,M_k),(M_{k+1},M_k),(0,mu)}; and the four silence identities Lambda(P_k)(v_1,a_{1,1}) = 2^{-e} M_k > 0, Lambda(P_k)(v_1,b_1) >= gamma + mu/2, Lambda(P_k)(a_{1,1},v_1) = Lambda(P_k)(b_1,v_1) = 0. I also re-derived every displayed inequality of the proof by hand and each is correct.

findings.defect: On WD the "free Z-seed" is vacuous, so the family does not test the seed that the standing rule of rem:own-stall makes part of the test.
findings.evidence: Z_0 = {t_0} and Z_1 = {t_1} on WD(4,2,6), WD(6,3,7), WD(8,4,8) and WD(3,2,4) (a22_wedgeQ.py), so the seed adds no row and Q(WD;L,U) = Q(WD). Confirmed: the shifted polytope Q(WD) - val equals P_0 = {xi in [0,1/2]^2 : xi_1 >= lambda xi_2 - 2 gamma, xi_2 >= lambda xi_1 - 2 gamma} exactly, vertex for vertex, in all four cases -- so rem:wedge's description of the wedge is right.

findings.defect: "the min-times closure of def:ratio first fires at rounds 30 and 87 for j = 2,3 and not within 170 rounds for j = 4" does not say which variant was measured; the harness measures the sound UPWARD-ROUNDED variant, and rounding up can only delay a firing.
findings.evidence: The project's t_wdratio.py runs mintimes_close_r with make_round(2a+2, 2^a), the rounded variant that prop:ratio-closure (line 8688, just outside this range) does declare and does caveat ("Rounding up can only delay a firing, so the counts are upper bounds ... the exact one is impractical here"). rem:wedge repeats the numbers without the caveat, so "not within 170 rounds for j = 4" is not evidence that the EXACT closure is silent for 170 rounds. I did not recompute these three numbers. I did recompute the def:trans-slack comparison numbers and they are right: first own-successor firing at 21 (j=2) and 51 (j=3) (a23_wedgeother.py); j=4 (claim 112) did not finish in budget.

findings.defect: "every hard family in this document has |C| <= 2" omits the two stall INSTANCES of this section and sec:simorder that have more.
findings.evidence: R of prop:own-stall (the one genuine decision stall of def:transport) has |C| = 5, and G* of prop:simorder-stalls, on which the primal-dual bracket separates none of its seven controlled vertices, has |C| = 7. Both verified. The remark's own conclusion (thm:lasserre-vacuous, with |C| = 3 witnesses, touches none of them) survives.

findings.defect: "note that (i) is non-strict, a weaker demand than the strict inequality the pair test needs" is a convention, not a fact, and thm:transport-barrier itself uses the non-strict form of the pair test.
findings.evidence: At v in Vmax, Delta(v^(0),v^(1)) <= 0 already proves w*(v^(0)) <= w*(v^(1)) and hence that v^(1) is optimal; no strictness is needed. thm:transport-barrier's statement is "the certificate decides the pair (a,b_0) if and only if bar t <= t_rev", i.e. Sep(a,b_0) <= 0, non-strict.

findings.defect: Two supporting statements are asserted rather than proved.
findings.evidence: (i) "every proof in sec:operators, sec:stopping uses only that sinks are absorbing and carry FIXED payoffs, never that those payoffs are 0 and 1" -- a global claim about other sections; the only place it is made precise is lem:gen-comparison, and only for T. (ii) "for dyadic theta the construction is literal, replacing u by an average vertex both of whose edges enter a chain of average vertices realising theta from t_0,t_1" -- the binary-expansion chain is described in prose only and is nowhere verified (the project's own standing note records that a route needing it must implement and verify it). Neither affects thm:fold, which I verified completely: for D = 1..10 the identity val_{P_D[u:=theta]}(F_D) = 2^{-(D+1)}(theta + 1 - 2^{-D} + 2^{-D} T^D(theta)) holds at every dyadic grid point, every midpoint and five off-grid rationals against backward induction, with 0 mismatches; slope set exactly {0, 2^{-D}}; exactly 2^D pieces and 2^D - 1 breakpoints; |V| = 6D+2 (a10_fold.py).

findings.defect: Two hypothesis-labelling slips that the proofs do not actually need.
findings.evidence: (a) thm:seeded-sound says "For every SSG and every bracket (L,U)" and "No stopping hypothesis is used", but "bracket" in def:bracket means L <= TL and TU <= U, from which L <= w* <= U follows only for stopping games (cor:comparison); what is used is def:seeded's hypothesis L <= w* <= U. (b) def:hybrid takes Z_0, Z_1 "as in def:simorder", which is stated for stopping G and asserts linear-time attractor computability, while thm:hybrid-sound claims no stopping hypothesis; soundness needs only Z_0 subset of {w* = 0} and Z_1 subset of {w* = 1}, but the linear-time computation is not justified off the stopping case.

findings.defect: Two measurement claims do not say what the instance generator varied, which the project's own standing rule requires.
findings.evidence: "Verified on 100 stopping games with |C| <= 5, all 2^{|C|} profiles of each" (no generator, no size distribution); "Random and hill-climbed search over games of this size never exceeded three rounds" (no generator, no count). Also unreproducible from the text: rem:hybrid-rate's two alternative constructions, described only in prose ("lengthening a single cycle joining a Max vertex to a Min vertex ... values are 1/3 and 2/3 for every k"). The explicit nine-vertex W of the same remark IS reproducible and exact: w* = (1/4,1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2), box widths 10/11, 1/5, 0, full hybrid collapses at round 3, sink-only at round 7 (a16.py) -- all as stated.

findings.defect: Notation collision: G_{\#} here (seven average vertices) and G^{\sharp} elsewhere (the 99-vertex two-player game realising the height-7 4-cube) both read as "G-sharp".
findings.evidence: Line 8760 defines G_{\#}; line 3944 defines G^{\sharp}. The macros differ (\# vs \sharp) but the names do not, and both are referred to as G-sharp in the round summaries.
